S046.name: Body_Image_Weight_Shape_Disturbance
S046.description: Undue influence of body weight or shape on self-evaluation.

subtypes.Distorted Body Image: Perceiving one's body as much fatter than it actually is or perceiving specific parts as excessively large when looking in the mirror.
subtypes.Self-Worth Dependent on Weight: Judging whether one is a good or successful person solely based on weight or body shape.

S047.name: Compensatory_Behavior_NonPurging
S047.description: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors to prevent weight gain without purging (direct removal of food).

subtypes.Fasting: Intentionally stopping food intake for a certain period to prevent weight gain.
subtypes.Excessive Exercise: Repetitively performing exercise at a level that exceeds physical limits to prevent weight gain.

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
examples: Eating more than 3-4 times the amount of a typical meal within 2 hours.
Continuously eating large amounts of high-calorie snacks in addition to main meals.
Eating enough to empty a significant portion of the refrigerator or pantry at once.
Eating clearly more food than others during the same period of time.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
examples: A feeling that once I start eating, I cannot stop even if I want to.
Thinking 'I shouldn't eat any more' but mechanically continuing to eat.
A feeling of helplessness that I cannot decide for myself how much to eat.
Eating as if my body is being controlled by someone else.

patient_info.stressor: When Ariana’s insurance agency reorganized its regional sales structure and asked senior agents to take on a more visible mentoring and life-and-health expansion role, she became unusually focused on looking polished and energetic in client events, leadership meetings, and community presentations. Over the next 4 months, her long workdays and Harvest Festival obligations led to repeated evenings in which she ate far more than planned after holding herself to strict daytime rules, followed by extra hiking, prolonged softball conditioning, or skipped meals to offset the fear of weight gain. Although she kept functioning well at work and at home, her sense of professional confidence became increasingly tied to whether her clothes fit the way she wanted before public-facing events. She brought it up during a routine primary-care visit after asking for a referral to someone who understood eating concerns without assuming purging was involved.

S046.name: Body_Image_Weight_Shape_Disturbance
S046.description: Undue influence of body weight or shape on self-evaluation.
S046.manifestation: If my waistband feels tight before a client luncheon or a leadership meeting, I start feeling like I look sloppy and like people won't take me as seriously, even though I know I've still been doing my job.

S047.name: Compensatory_Behavior_NonPurging
S047.description: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors to prevent weight gain without purging (direct removal of food).
S047.manifestation: The next day after one of those nights, I'll tell myself I'm making up for it by skipping breakfast and lunch or taking an extra-long hike or pushing harder at softball conditioning, even when I'm tired.

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
S049.manifestation: What brought me in is that some evenings after work, especially when I've been strict all day, I end up eating way more than I meant to, like dinner, then cereal, crackers, leftovers, and sweets all within a couple hours.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
S050.manifestation: Once I get started on those nights, it's like I keep going back to the kitchen even while I'm telling myself to stop, and I don't really feel back in charge until I'm uncomfortably full.

additional_requirement_1.name: Additional Requirement 1
additional_requirement_1.description: The binge eating and inappropriate compensatory behaviors both occur, on average, at least once a week for 3 months
additional_requirement_1.manifestation: For the past few months, this has been happening most weeks—usually one or two nights where I eat far more than I planned, and then the next day I try to make up for it by skipping meals or exercising longer.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: I’m still keeping up with my clients, mentoring role, and home responsibilities, but I sometimes feel distracted and less confident before public events if I’m worried about how my clothes fit.

duration.name: Duration
duration.manifestation: This started after the agency’s regional sales reorganization about four months ago.
